notes: Exists for the two pyspark signatures that differ between Spark 3.5 and 4.x, not for new Informatica behaviour. SUBSTR with a computed bound emits Column.substr(Column, Column); a literal bound emits F.substring(col, int, int); INDEXOF emits a CASE chain. In pyspark 4 F.substring and F.array_position accept a Column and in 3.5 they do not, so the 4-only forms pass locally on 4.x and raise 'Column is not iterable' on AIDP. Both were live-only findings (PRs #5, #6).
EMAIL_DOMAIN = SUBSTR(EMAIL, INSTR(EMAIL,'@')+1). INSTR is 1-based and returns 0 when absent, so row 3 ('no-at-sign') gets start 1 and the whole string back -- not an empty string.
EMAIL_LOCAL guards the no-'@' case with IIF so the length is never negative: IIF(INSTR>0, SUBSTR(EMAIL,1,INSTR-1), EMAIL). Row 3 therefore returns EMAIL unchanged.
A NULL EMAIL makes INSTR NULL, so 'NULL > 0' is unknown and the IIF takes its else branch -- EMAIL, which is NULL. Row 4 is NULL for both email ports.

COLOUR_RANK = INDEXOF(COLOUR,'red','green','blue') is 1-based, 0 when nothing matches (row 5 'purple'), and NULL for a NULL input (row 4). Only exact lower-case values are used, so the CaseFlag default is not relied on.
ZIP3 = SUBSTR(ZIP,1,3) keeps the literal-bound form in the same case, so a regression that broke only one of the two emitted shapes would still be caught.

Deliberately NOT covered: a leading '@' would make SUBSTR(EMAIL,1,0) -- whether Informatica returns an empty string or NULL for a zero length is not something this project has verified, so no row relies on it.
